en.title: k-th Smallest Element of Every Window of Length m
en.description:
For each contiguous window of length m in the array, from left to right, output its k-th smallest element; equal numbers at different positions each take their own rank. Output in increasing order of window start. The original statement was truncated; this rule is restored from what the original example states explicitly: windows of m=3, the 2nd smallest, and the output order.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m k; the second line contains the array. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤k≤m≤n≤100000, −10^9≤element≤10^9.
en.output: Output n−m+1 integers in order of window start, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The answers are 3 2, 2 2 and −5. In the second example the two 2s are two separate elements.
hints: Compress the values and maintain the frequency of each value in the current window with a Fenwick tree. Use binary lifting to find the position where the prefix frequency first reaches k; when sliding, remove the old element and add the new one.
